q1_issues.issue: The explicit universal object "all the local waters" is encoded only as a single group filler (Patient = sk_waters_1), so "all" never becomes a quantified range, whereas the instruction set turns an explicit universal into a per-member distribution premise (and a second-quantifier clause into a rule premise).
The QuantifierPhrase companion names the range kind `water`, but no premise of the rule quantifies over water, so the companion annotates a quantified range that does not exist in the parse.

q2_gaps: episodic/existential bare-plural subject under a present perfect ("Fishing trawlers HAVE fished out ..." reports what actual trawlers did, not a characterizing generic): the instruction set offers only the generic distribution rule for a bare plural or a group witness for a definite plural, with no existential bare-plural form, so an arbitrary fishing trawler anywhere inherits the fishing-out at 0.9
notes: The phrasal verb kept whole as `fish_out` with no genus, the `fishing_trawler` compound genus with the noun modifier left unexposed, the definite-plural group witness, and the distribution rule for the descriptive modifier "local" all follow the instruction set.
